name: Ukraine (since 1991)
summary: Independent since the Soviet Union broke up in 1991. Russia annexed Crimea in 2014 and launched a full-scale invasion in 2022.

knownFor.label: Black earth (chornozem)
knownFor.note: Very fertile soil; a major grain exporter.

knownFor.label: Chernobyl disaster
knownFor.note: The worst nuclear accident, while Ukraine was Soviet.

location.value: Eastern Europe on the Black Sea; about 604,000 km² (internationally recognised borders).

terrain.value: Plains and steppe; the Carpathians in the west.

climate.value: Continental, with cold winters, warm summers and a milder Black Sea coast and Crimean peninsula.

resources.value: Very fertile black-earth farmland, iron ore, coal and titanium.

disasters.value: The Chernobyl disaster (26 April 1986), the worst nuclear reactor accident in history.

population.value: Around 32 million people, far fewer than before the 2022 invasion.

urbanisation.value: Kyiv is the capital and largest city, followed by Kharkiv, Odesa and Dnipro.

disease.value: Health care has been disrupted by the war, with many hospitals damaged.

economicBase.value: Grain and sunflower oil exports, steel, IT services.

tradeRoutes.value: Black Sea ports such as Odesa carry grain exports; the 2022 invasion blocked them and a grain corridor was agreed in 2022–23.

wealth.value: A lower-middle-income country, hard hit by the war.

moneyAndTax.value: The hryvnia, which fell sharply in late 1998.

inequality.value: Wealth was concentrated among a few oligarchs before the war, and many people have been displaced since.

keyRulers.value: Leonid Kravchuk. Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: Presidents are elected, and power has changed hands after the Orange Revolution (2004) and the Maidan protests (2014).

institutions.value: The Verkhovna Rada (parliament); the constitution was adopted on 28 June 1996.

stability.value: The Orange Revolution (2004) and the Euromaidan revolution (2014).

eliteConflict.value: Rival political groups and business-linked elites have competed for power, with debates about ties to Russia or Europe.

majorWars.value: The Russo-Ukrainian War since 2014; Russia’s full-scale invasion began a new phase in 2022.

territoryChange.value: Russia annexed Crimea (2014) and claims four more regions (2022). Ukraine and most countries regard these annexations as illegal; Russia says Crimea’s 2014 referendum was an act of self-determination.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Ukraine; Wikipedia: Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation (checked 18 Nov 2026)

alliancesRivals.value: Declared itself neutral at independence (1991); granted EU candidate status on 23 June 2022.

inventions.value: The Antonov aircraft design bureau (including the huge An-225) and a rocket industry came from Ukraine.

scienceEducation.value: Literacy is almost universal, with strong schools in engineering and sciences.

openness.value: Open to Europe and the West, with the EU association agreement and candidate status (2022).

communicationTransport.value: Railways carry most long-distance passengers and goods, and many were damaged by the war.

religion.value: Mostly Orthodox Christian, with Greek Catholic, Muslim (Crimean Tatar) and Jewish minorities.

languageWriting.value: Ukrainian is the official language; Russian is widely spoken, especially in the east and south.

artsArchitecture.value: The national poet Taras Shevchenko (1814–61), who led the national movement with Mykhailo Drahomanov.

socialStructure.value: Large gaps opened after the war, with millions displaced inside the country and abroad.

dailyLife.value: Many people live in apartment blocks or houses and eat borscht, varenyky and bread.

neighbours.value: Russia, Belarus, Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, Moldova.

ideasReligions.value: European integration and national sovereignty have become central political ideas.

colonisation.value: Part of the Soviet Union until it gained independence in 1991.

riseSignals.value: Gained independence in 1991 as the Soviet Union dissolved.

peakPeriod.value: Growth in the 2000s, when the economy expanded rapidly before the 2008 crisis.

outcome.value: Ukraine continues as an independent state, at war since 2022.

overallCertainty.value: War casualty and population figures are disputed.
